simple.meaning: בְּלִיל (bᵉlîyl) is a Hebrew word meaning “mixed , i.e. (specifically) feed (for cattle).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: בְּלִיל (H1098) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 6:5, with occurrences in Job, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בְּלִיל (H1098) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in בְּלִיל (H1098) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: בְּלִיל (bᵉlîyl) / H1098 is traced through Job 6:5, Job 24:6, Isaiah 30:24 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1098. belil בְּלִיל noun masculine Isa 30:24 fodder (Aramaic ; compare Arabic moisture of fresh pasture ) — בְּלִיל 30:24 ; suffix בְּלִילוֺ Job 6:5 ; 24:6 — fodder (strictly, mixed fodder, farrago ) 6:5 ; as growing in field 24:6 compare Isa 30:24 .

occurrences.englishText: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass?
They cut their food in the field.
The oxen likewise and the young donkeys that till the ground will eat savory feed, which has been winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.
